reuse.why: Reuses getRangedAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a new getExpectedAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount (which already decides missing/number/range) instead of extending it with the operator.

duplication.why: Consolidates four server-side inline dispatches into one helper, but that helper re-implements getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch, leaving two parallel definitions of the expected amount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the other amount helpers and server modules import it.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule; the extra _amountOp field and fallback in forecast normalizeSchedule are needed plumbing.

maintainability.why: Server paths are now uniform, but API expectedAmount (api-models.ts) and all client consumers still use getScheduledAmount without the approximate rule, so two helpers now disagree.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts is created alongside getScheduledAmount instead of extending it; api-models.ts expectedAmount and desktop-client consumers keep using getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount's 'null -> 0, non-number -> getRangedAmount, number -> value' is getScheduledAmount's dispatch reshaped with early returns and an op parameter instead of inverse

one_place.where: Server paths (schedule-template, forecast normalizeSchedule, schedules/app updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions) use getExpectedAmount, but api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal expectedAmount and the client use getScheduledAmount, which ignores the approximate rule
